suggestions.issue: <image> #1 (href='../media/image1.gif') has no alt text — required for accessibility
context_lines: Documents may contain images. For example, there is an image of the web accessibility symbol to the left of this paragraph. Its alternate text is "Web Access Symbol".
Alt text should communicate what an image means, not how it looks.

Some images, such as charts or graphs, require long descriptions, but not all document types allow that. In web pages, long descriptions may be provided in several ways: on the page below the image, via a link below the image, or via a link on the image.
suggestions.suggestion:
<image> #1 (href='../media/image1.gif') has no alt text — required for accessibility.
Add an `alt` attribute to the `<image>` element with a brief description of what the image shows.
Example: `<image href='../media/image.png' alt='Description of image content'/>`

context_lines: This is an example of columns. With columns, the page is split into two or more horizontal sections. Unlike tables, in which you usually read across a row and then down to the next, in columns, you read down a column and then across to the next.

When columns are not created correctly, screen readers may run lines together, reading the first line of the first column, then the first line of the second column, then the second line of the first column, and so on. Obviously, that is not accessible.
